title: The UCSD Microbiome and Metagenomics Center
text:
The proposed Microbiome and Metagenomics Center is relevant to human health because we anticipate results
can be used by the Nutrition for Precision Health Consortium to understand the relationship between the
microbiome, nutrition, and human health. Data and technologies developed will be widely available to the
community to promote further scientific advances. The Center is relevant to NIH and NIDDK’s mission because
it seeks to produce high quality metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data that will help determine how nutrition
and the microbiome can be used to improve people’s health and quality of life.

title: Imaging with high chemical and spatial resolutions using mass spectrometry
text:
Biomedical imaging provides important functional, metabolic, and molecular information to scientists and
physicians to facilitate a wide variety of basic, diagnostic, and therapeutic applications. In particular, molecular
imaging at high chemical resolution offers the opportunity to discover novel biomarkers and mechanisms of
disease, while molecular imaging at high spatial resolutions offers the opportunity to directly measure changing
concentrations of molecules in exceedingly small areas within and between individual cells. Our lab proposes to
develop novel instrumentation, gas-phase reactions, sample preparation protocols, and computational strategies
to enable unique molecular imaging technologies in a wide variety of biomedical research settings, such as in
studies of infectious disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration, and cancer.

title: Integrative Multidisciplinary Discovery Platform to Unlock Marine Natural Products Therapeutic Opportunities
text:
The genomes of cyanobacteria and sponge-associated microbes encode numerous compounds that could
provide the basis for new drugs. Discovery and development of these chemicals as drug candidates, however,
is challenging due to their low availability in Nature. The proposed multidisciplinary research will address this
limitation and should provide the methodology to increase the number of new natural products as starting points
for drug discovery and development.

title: The nose-lung cross talk in upper respiratory virus infection induced asthma exacerbations
text:
Upper respiratory virus infection (URVI) is responsible for 80% of asthma attacks; however, the underlying
mechanisms remain poorly understood. This project is proposed to dissect the cellular and molecular
mechanisms undelying the nose -lung cross talk, particularly how URVI causes asthma attacks. Findings from
this research are expected to lead to not only novel preventive and therapeutic strategies for asthmatics, but
also to define nasal mucosal immune system and subsequently facilitate nasal vaccine development against
airborne pathogens.

title: A kinetic framework to map the genetic determinants of alternative RNA isoform expression
text:
The biogenesis of mRNA is a complex and highly regulated process, requiring coordination between transcrip-
tional and RNA processing machinery that each comprise of hundreds of regulatory RNAs and proteins, resulting
in many possible alternative isoforms expressed from a single gene. While we can now extensively catalog the
abundance and variability of mRNA isoforms across cellular states, we are still limited in our abilities to predict
coordination between the molecular steps that give rise to cellular diversity and the rates at which each of these
mechanisms occurs. Here, we propose to generate checkpointed time-series RNA-sequencing data and robust
statistical models to quantify RNA processing rates, fully characterize the kinetic competition underlying alterna-
tive isoform expression, and identify genetic variants associated with variabilty in RNA processing rates across
human cell lines.

title: SUNBEAM Birth Cohort: Deciphering the role of early life skin dysfunction in development of the allergic march
text:
Atopic dermatitis (AD) and food allergy are among the most common chronic diseases of early childhood. These
diseases often occur in the same individuals and many times lead to the development of hay fever and asthma,
in a poorly understood process termed the allergic march. In this project we will investigate whether early-life
barrier and immune abnormalities of the skin result in not only AD, but affect the overall immune system, leading
to the allergic march.

title: Linking microbes to cardiovascular-associated metabolites using knowledge-based machine learning
text:
The gut microbiome produces metabolites that directly influence the development of cardiovascular disease
(CVD), but we currently have no reliable way to determine how we could manipulate the microbiome to improve
cardiovascular health. This project will utilize state-of-the-art protein language models to identify metabolic
enzymes in over 200,000 gut bacterial genomes, develop machine learning frameworks that can predict the
metabolite production of bacterial communities, and analyze 10,000 CVD patients to identify microbial drivers of
their disease. By establishing mechanistic links between specific microbes, metabolites, and CVD outcomes,
this work will enable precision microbiome therapies that reduce CVD morbidity and mortality.

title: Improved Methods and Commercialization of a Multimodal Vibrating Sharp-Edge Spray Ionization Source
text:
The proposed work will produce a disruptive product, the Spanda MultimodalTM ionization source. This source
will replace the top three selling ionization sources that are utilized by high-end mass spectrometers in many
different types of analytical laboratories. The new source will provide cost savings to customers with much
improved performance (e.g., throughput, sensitivity, and functionality).

title: Targeting dsRNA sensing and ADAR1 in melanoma
text:
Targeting dsRNA pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) in tumors represents a promising strategy to treat
patients with melanoma and other tumor types. In this proposal we address gaps in knowledge that limit the
translation of dsRNA PRR-targeting strategies, determining the effects of dsRNA sensing on T cells, evaluating
the efficacy of targeting single versus multiple sensing pathways and identifying the tumors most likely to
respond to therapy. If successful, this work will help define the rules that govern tumor and immune responses
to dsRNA and advance novel therapeutic strategies that target RIG-I and ADAR1.

title: Mechanisms of NBR2, a Long Non-Coding RNA, in Human Ovarian Aging
text:
This project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying ovarian aging by investigating the role of the
long non-coding RNA, NBR2, and its regulatory variant, which is associated with later age at natural menopause
and longer reproductive lifespan. I will investigate how NBR2 regulates pro-longevity signaling pathways and
ovarian cell function and how the regulatory variant alters NBR2 expression through changes in transcription
factor binding and chromatin architecture. This research will advance our understanding of the genetic and
molecular drivers of ovarian aging and may lead to new intervention strategies to promote reproductive longevity
and healthspan in women.

title: Precision Medicine in Prediabetes: Identifying Cardiometabolic Subtypes to Improve Risk Stratification
text:
Prediabetes is defined based solely on glycemic biomarkers, but there is substantial variation in
pathophysiology, cardiometabolic risk factor profiles, and prognosis among people with prediabetes. We will
use state-of-the-art methods to classify individuals with prediabetes into clusters with distinct cardiometabolic
risk profiles with varying risks of diabetes and complications.

title: Precision Targeting of Hippocampal Subfields with AAVs
text:
The hippocampus is responsible for key memory functions and spatial navigation and is a focal point of several
neurodegenerative diseases such as epilepsy and Alzheimer’s disease, affecting millions of people worldwide.
Developments from this proposal will lead to novel and potentially therapeutic tool development for a fuller
understanding of basic neuronal function in hippocampus.

title: Developing allogeneic iNKT cell adoptive therapy to improve outcomes for HSCT indications
text:
Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT) is a life-saving treatment for multiple chronic debilitating
diseases, including blood cancers, immunodeficiencies, and certain viral infections. However, HSCT is limited
by several critical problems, including failure of the graft to take hold, and attack of patient tissues by graft
cells. MiNK Therapeutics has developed a cellular immunotherapy (agenT-797) composed of a highly
specialized immune population called invariant Natural Killer T (iNKT) cells, that has shown promise for
treating immune disorders in other disease settings. This project investigates the potential of agenT-797 to
enhance the success of HSCT by inhibiting attack of patient tissues and promoting successful immune
repopulation by graft cells. Completion of these studies will provide key data to support the clinical application
of agenT-797 in HSCT procedures.

title: IL17 dependent angiocrine signaling drives inflammation in alcohol associated hepatitis
text:
Alcoholic hepatitis is a disease of intense liver inflammation and injury caused by heavy alcohol use that can be
deadly when severe. Cytokine IL17 may contribute to the development of alcoholic hepatitis by stimulating liver
sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) to produce chemokines that drives the inflammatory response. In this study,
we will explore the mechanisms of IL17-mediated LSEC activation in alcoholic hepatitis and experiment with
novel ways of inhibiting IL17 production by targeting a gene regulatory element.

title: ENaC regulation and its role in blood pressure homeostasis
text:
Epithelial sodium channels (ENaCs) are expressed in distal aspects of the nephron and facilitate the reabsorption
of filtered sodium from kidney tubules, thereby regulating body sodium content, fluid volume and blood pressure.
ENaCs are expressed at other sites that influence blood pressure, including antigen presenting dendritic cells
and monocytes where they have a role in linking a high salt diet, inflammation and blood pressure. Proposed
studies will delineate the roles of specific ENaC subunits and key ENaC regulators in dendritic cell and monocyte
activation and blood pressure.

title: Linking Genetic and Clinical Data to Optimize Surgical Opioid Analgesic Prescribing and Predict Risks of Opioid-Related Adverse Drug Events
text:
This proposal aims to quantitatively evaluate effects of opioid drugs on post-surgical pain relief and risk of
opioid-related adverse drug events using patient-level clinical and genetic information. Statistical and machine
learning models will be developed to recommend optimal opioid prescription dosage (oral morphine milligram
equivalents). Polygenic risk score will be built to represent patients' genetic susceptibility to the given post-
surgical opioid prescription-related outcomes and identify high-risk patient populations.

title: Daily experiences and cognitive mediators of behavioral obesity treatment outcomes
text: A significant proportion of individuals who enroll in behavioral weight loss interventions do not achieve clinically meaningful weight reductions. This project will characterize the mechanisms through which adverse daily experiences and present bias -- a cognitive tendency to prioritize immediate needs over long-term goals -- account for variation in weight loss outcomes.

title: Toward Personalized Prognosis and Outcomes in Primary Progressive Aphasia
text:
Primary progressive aphasia (PPA), a devastating neurodegenerative syndrome that
involves relentless development of language impairment, is currently not treatable in part
because of a lack of tools available for identifying the underlying molecular diagnosis
and for monitoring patients. This project aims to employ and validate new imaging
methods for use as markers in clinical research and care, one goal of which is to serve
as markers to determine whether potential therapies are effective.

title: Resources and Workforce Development for the Regional Biocontainment Laboratories
text:
The Duke Regional Biocontainment Laboratory was commissioned in 2007 as a part of a network of 12 RBLs
tasked with providing state-of-the-art facilities to aid in the response emerging pathogens and pandemic
preparedness. This grant will provide critical support of the RBL operational infrastructure, comprehensive
training program, and enhancement of Research Support services.

title: Molecular Biology and Genetics of Human Tumor Viruses
text:
OVERALL – PROJECT NARRATIVE
Viruses contribute to at least 21 different human cancers, representing approximately 15% of all human cancers.
Understanding the biology of these human tumor viruses and how they cause cancer will provide new
approaches for preventing and treating the associated cancers. In this program project grant a highly interactive
group of seven investigators and their laboratory members engage in collaborative research focused on two
objectives: to elucidate the life cycles of and transformation by human tumor viruses and to translate this
understanding into the identification of targets for specific anti-viral, anti-tumor therapies.
